title: Composition isomorphism for pullbacks
statement:
For morphisms $h_1\colon T\to S$ and $h_2\colon S\to R$, the *composition isomorphism*
of pullbacks

$$
(h_2\circ h_1)^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }h_1^*\circ h_2^*
$$

is the conjugate (the mate with identity intervening functors of
[def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]), under the adjunctions of
[def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], of the composition
isomorphism $(h_2)_*\circ(h_1)_*\cong(h_2\circ h_1)_*$ of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp].

proof.text:
Put $L_1=(h_2\circ h_1)^*$, $R_1=(h_2\circ h_1)_*$, $L_2=h_1^*\circ h_2^*$ and $R_2=(h_2)_*\circ(h_1)_*$. By [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], $L_1\dashv R_1$, $h_2^*\dashv(h_2)_*$ and $h_1^*\dashv(h_1)_*$. Apply [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] to the last two adjunctions. Its Hom bijection is
$$\operatorname{Hom}(h_1^*h_2^*F,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_2^*F,(h_1)_*G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,(h_2)_*(h_1)_*G),$$
so it supplies $L_2\dashv R_2$. Denote the units of these two adjunctions by $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$, and the counit of the first by $\varepsilon_1$.

source.place: sole proof paragraph, composite adjunction and compatible uniqueness

proof.text:
Let $\delta:R_2\xrightarrow{\sim}R_1$ be the pushforward composition isomorphism of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp], in its displayed direction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to the adjunctions of Step 1 and to $\delta$. It gives a unique natural transformation $c:L_1\to L_2$ satisfying
$$R_1(c_F)\circ\eta_{1,F}=\delta_{L_2F}\circ\eta_{2,F},$$
and states that $c$ is a natural isomorphism. Its direction is precisely $(h_2\circ h_1)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_1^*\circ h_2^*$.

source.place: sole proof paragraph, composite adjunction and compatible uniqueness

proof.text:
Specialize [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] to identity intervening functors, taking its first adjunction to be $L_2\dashv R_2$ and its second to be $L_1\dashv R_1$. Its inverse mate sends $\delta:R_2\to R_1$ to the transformation with component
$$m_F=\varepsilon_{1,L_2F}\circ L_1(\delta_{L_2F}\circ\eta_{2,F}).$$
Write $a_F=\delta_{L_2F}\circ\eta_{2,F}$. Naturality of $\eta_1$ and the triangle identity give
$$R_1(m_F)\circ\eta_{1,F}=R_1(\varepsilon_{1,L_2F})\circ R_1L_1(a_F)\circ\eta_{1,F}=R_1(\varepsilon_{1,L_2F})\circ\eta_{1,R_1L_2F}\circ a_F=a_F.$$
Thus $m$ has the unit equation of Step 2 and equals $c$ by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. This proves the defining conjugate characterization with the forward pushforward compositor. The inverse pushforward compositor has the reverse pullback mate, so its mate must be inverted to obtain $c$.

lean.note: Exact existing composition isomorphism for pullbacks on small pro-étale sheaves. Its definition applies the inverse conjugateIsoEquiv under the composite-morphism adjunction and the composite adjunction to (lowerStarComp A h₁ h₂).symm, and then inverts the result. Thus the hom is the mate of the forward pushforward compositor, as explicitly confirmed by conjugateEquiv_upperStarComp_hom in UpperLowerStar.Iso. Parameters: A : Type u' with Category.{u + 1} A, Abelian A, and IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1} A; arbitrary h₁ : T ⟶ S and h₂ : S ⟶ R for Scheme.{u}. The full declarations were read in the pinned slopmaster2 checkout and the project-side pro-etale framework.
